summary_out.hypothesis: Gen-1 migration's `generalizable` finding said spread-quantile (book-state, island-0 winner) and chop-ratio (price-path, island-2 winner) skip gates target near-orthogonal adverse-microstructure regimes and should compose across bases. g2l1 confirmed the spread+flow pair on this base (+70.29% vs base). This loop tested whether ADDING a third structurally distinct skip axis (chop, the price-path axis) on top of an unmodified spread+flow stack continues to compound, or whether marginal axes are redundant past two. Verdict: CONFIRMED with strong magnitude. The three-gate stack delivered a 1.7x amplification of the spread+flow improvement for an incremental ~5% trade_count cost, with drawdown TIGHTENING further and sharpe rising +4.58 absolute — evidence that the chop-skip set is approximately independent of (spread-skip ∪ flow-skip), i.e. the three axes are genuinely orthogonal on this base.
